images.caption: View of a mannequin depicting the extraction (or tapping) of natural latex (used for making rubber) in what is now Malaysia, on display in Gallery C (Colonial Era) at the National Museum (Malaysia). The tapping process starts early in the morning (as early as 2 am) and continues until the latex stops flowing by about noon. The tapper returns a few hours later and empties the latex into a tin container.
images.alt: View of a mannequin depicting the extraction (or tapping) of natural latex (used for making rubber) in what is now Malaysia, on display in Gallery C (Colonial Era) at the National Museum (Malaysia). images.caption:
Bronze bell. Klang, Selangor state, western Malaysia. About 200 BCE-200 CE.
Found with a number of iron tools, this bell is one of the only two examples of the type, the other from Battambang in Cambodia. It is probably a ceremonial object related to the bronze drums known from many regions of southeast Asia and south China. British Museum.
images.alt:

images.caption: The signing of the Cobbold Report of the Commission of Enquiry, North Borneo and Sarawak, at Knebworth House, London on 21 June 1962. The Commission consists of five members, and is chaired by Lord Cobbold, a former governor of the Bank of England.  Its other members are Dato' Wong Pow Nee and Encik Mohd Ghazali bin Shafie, representing the government of Malaya, Sir Anthony Abell, and Sir David Watherston, the representative of the British government. Mr. H. Harris acted as the Secretary.
images.alt: The signing of the Cobbold Report of the Commission of Enquiry, North Borneo and Sarawak, at Knebworth House, London on 21 June 1962.
